The SPV module API reference¶

Mean Square Displacement calculator If the seed points identity is conserved throughout the iterations (which is most likely the case visually, due to our colour trackers), then we can just parse the seed_point_log and compute difference in position from it ?). This will have to take into account periodic boundary displacement.

MSD.MSD_analysis()¶

Opens the necessary logs to compute the MSD

Parameters:
  • logfilename (string) – Name of the logfile containing the parameters for the experiment (already joined with the path)
  • velocities_log_filename (string) – Name of the file containing the log for the velocity of every cell at each iteration (already joined with the path)
Returns:

MSD_vector – Vector with the Mean Sqaured Displacement at every iteration
Return type:

np array
MSD.compute_MSD()¶

Basic version without computation within the center of mass frame

Parameters:
  • point_number (int) – Number of cells in the system
  • delta_t (float) – Timestep between two computations
  • iteration_number (int) – Number of iteration of computation in the system
  • velocities (numpy array) – Array containing the velocities logged for each cell at every iteration
Returns:

MSD_vector – The i-th element is the MSD at the i-th iteration
Return type:

numpy array of iteration_number elements
MSD.compute_MSD_bad()¶

[DEPRECATED] Compute the Mean Square Displacement : 1/N * (sum_n->N (x_n(t) - x_n(0)**2)

Parameters:states (numpy array) – States extracted from a seed_point_log.csv file recording position of seed points at every iteration
Returns:MSD – Mean Square Displacement of every voronoi cell over time
Return type:numpy array
MSD.compute_MSD_center_mass()¶

Version with computation within the center of mass frame

Parameters:
  • point_number (int) – Number of cells in the system
  • delta_t (float) – Timestep between two computations
  • iteration_number (int) – Number of iteration of computation in the system
  • velocities (numpy array) – Array containing the velocities logged for each cell at every iteration
Returns:

MSD_vector – The i-th element is the MSD at the i-th iteration
Return type:

numpy array of iteration_number elements
MSD.compute_MSD_velocity()¶

[DEPRECATED] Compute the Mean Square Displacement : 1/N * (sum_n->N [delta_t * (v_n(t) - v_n(0)**2)])

Parameters:
  • velocities (numpy array) – Velocity vectors for individual cells extracted from a velocities_log.csv file recording the velocity of each seed point at every iteration
  • numpy array (initial_positions) – Reference for the (x,y) positions of the seed points (at iteration 0 or )
Returns:

MSD – Mean Square Displacement of every voronoi cell over time
Return type:

numpy array
MSD.compute_nematic_scalar_quadrupole()¶

Compute the quadrupole (average of the second Legendre polynomial) as an orientational order parameter (as defined in De Gennes and Prost, The Physics of Liquid Crystals)

Returns:scalar_quadrupole – Orientational order parameter describing the alignement of liquid crystals
Return type:float

MSD.orientational_orders_analysis()¶

Opens the necessary logs to compute the orientational orders

Parameters:
  • logfilename (string) – Name of the logfile containing the parameters for the experiment (already joined with the path)
  • velocities_log_filename (string) – Name of the file containing the log for the velocity of every cell at each iteration (already joined with the path)
Returns:

Orientational orders – Order parameter of the system. The closer it is to 1, the more ordered the system is.
Return type:

np array

The “saucisse” module¶

Parameters generator. Generates a text file with the commands to insert in the job manager. Call with python3 parameters.generator.py parameter_to_explore min_parameter max_parameter step_size

parameters_generator.generate_parameters(filename, filename_prefix, parameter_to_explore, min_parameter, max_parameter, step_size)[source]¶

Creates a textfile containing commands for the job manager with a parameter to explore

Parameters:
  • filename (string) – Name of the file to register the commands and parameters
  • filename_prefix (string) – e.g. : “/opt/anaconda3/bin/python3 flocking_confluent_marchetti.py”
  • parameter_to_explore (string) – The parameter to vary, e.g. “point_number”, “boxsize”, “K_P”…
  • min_parameter (int, float) – Start value for the exploration
  • max_parameter (int, float) – End value for the exploration
  • step_size (int, float) – Increment size for the exploration
Returns:
Return type:

Nothing
parameters_generator.write_parameters_file(filename, filename_prefix, parameter_string)[source]¶

Concatenates a command prefix and the string of parameters to build a full command

Parameters:
  • filename (string) – Name of the file to write/append to
  • filename_prefix (string) – e.g. flocking_confluent_marchetti.py
  • parameter_string (string) – String of parameter to run the main script in the “Passed arguments mode”
Returns:
Return type:

Nothing
